Definition: from G5324; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. spectre:--spirit.
BiblicalUsage: Phantasma is an apparition, a spectre, a spirit, and it appears when the disciples see Jesus walking on the sea. They suppose it is a spirit and cry out for fear, until He speaks and says it is He.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that fear makes phantoms of everything, even of Jesus: the disciples saw their Lord and thought Him a ghost, until His voice told them who He was.
